summary: Michael Rostovtzeff was a historian and archaeologist working in Iranian and Central Asian studies. Educated at Kiev Gymnasium, Kyiv University, and St. Petersburg University, he held posts at St. Petersburg, Bestuzhev Courses, Oxford, Wisconsin-Madison, and Yale.

Michael S. Drummond is a scholar of Buddhist studies. He earned a Master of Arts in Buddhist Studies at the University of Bristol and pursued PhD studies at Utrecht University, where he was attested as a candidate in 2006.

Michael Schmidt specializes in Indology and Buddhist studies. He worked on the Katalogisierung der orientalischen Handschriften in Deutschland in 1992 and held posts as dictionary editor (attested 1981) and collaborator (attested 2008) at the Göttingen Academy of Sciences and Humanities.
Michael Silverstein was a linguist who studied at Stuyvesant High School and Harvard University (~1962–1971). He held an academic post at the University of Chicago from around 1970 until 2020.

Michael Stanley-Baker works in Sinology, religious studies, and history/archaeology. He earned an MA under Stephen R. Bokenkamp at Indiana University (attested 2006) and held posts at Pittsburgh, Nanyang Technological University, Leipzig University, and the Max Planck Institute.
Michael Torsten Much is a scholar of Indology, Tibetology, and Buddhist studies who studied under Ernst Steinkellner (attested 1991). He held a fellowship post at the University of Hamburg.

Michael Viggo Fausbøll was an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar. He studied theology and trained under Niels Ludvig Westergaard at the University of Copenhagen, where he served as an assistant librarian and later as Professor of Indian Philology (1878–1902).

Michael W. Meister is a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology. He completed his BA, MA, and PhD at Harvard University and studied at the University of Pennsylvania, where he served as a professor from circa 1976 to 2022.

Michael Weiers was a linguist and scholar of Iranian and Central Asian studies. He earned his doctorate at the University of Bonn by 1965 and served there as professor from 1972 to 2003, also holding an honorary professorship at Inner Mongolia University.

Michael Wenger is a Buddhist studies specialist who studied at The New School and trained under Sojun Mel Weitsman. He served as Dean of Buddhist Studies at San Francisco Zen Center (~1989) and founded Dragons Leap Meditation Center in 2012.

Michael Willis is a scholar of Indology, history, and archaeology. He studied at the University of Victoria and completed his doctorate at the University of Chicago in 1988, later serving as curator of South Asian Collections at the British Museum (1994–2014).

Michael Witzel is an Indologist and linguist who studied under Paul Thieme, Karl Hoffmann, and others. He led the Nepal Research Centre (1972–1978), held the Sanskrit chair at Leiden (1978–1986), and was appointed Sanskrit chair at Harvard in 1986.

Michael Zimmermann is a Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Indology scholar. He earned his PhD at the University of Hamburg, studied at Soka University, and later held posts including professor at Stanford (2003) and director at the University of Hamburg.

Michael von Brück is a scholar of religious studies, Buddhist studies, and Indology. He earned his doctorate at the University of Rostock (1968–1973) and held professorships at the University of Regensburg (1988–1991) and the University of Munich (~1991–2014).
Michaela Haas is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She earned her PhD at the University of Bonn under Peter Schwieger, having also studied under Rechungpa and Jigme Namgyel.

Michaela Mross specializes in Buddhist studies and Japanology. She studied at Komazawa University and the University of Munich (PhD, 2014), subsequently holding positions at UC Berkeley, the University of Göttingen, and Stanford University.

Michel Bitbol is a scholar in philosophy and Buddhist studies who studied at Paris Diderot University and under Pierre Mills. He held posts as directeur de recherche at CNRS (~1990) and at institutions including IHPST, Oxford, and École Normale Supérieure.

Michel Bréal was a linguist and Indologist who studied at École Normale Supérieure, the University of Berlin, and under Franz Bopp and Albrecht Weber. He served as a professor at Collège de France (1864–1905) and director at EPHE (~1868–1882).

Michel Clasquin-Johnson is a religious studies and Buddhist studies scholar. He completed undergraduate, graduate, and doctoral studies at the University of South Africa between circa 1989 and 1999, and held an academic post there starting in 1990.

Michel Hulin was a scholar of philosophy and Indology who studied at the École Normale Supérieure and Paris-Sorbonne University under Olivier Lacombe. He held a teaching post at Paris-Sorbonne University from 1981 to 1998.
